conditions.detail: Two-node DGX Spark cluster: ray head 192.168.1.11 (this box, harness ran here) + worker 192.168.1.2, one GB10 each, ray 2.57.0; the third node of the earlier TP=3 cluster (192.168.1.7) is not part of this ray cluster (verified via ray.nodes()). Head node additionally hosts an idle GNOME session (Xorg + gnome-shell), earlyoom, and two CPU-only containers started minutes before the run: open-webui and searxng (neither holds GPU memory - see isolation check). Ambient GPU state at start: 48C, 11W.
conditions.isolation_check: Measured, not asserted: nvidia-smi compute apps on the head node at run start = exactly one process (ray::RayWorkerProc.run, 94,199 MiB) - open-webui and searxng hold no GPU allocation. Ray cluster resource report: 2/2 GPUs reserved by this engine's placement group across both nodes, so no other GPU work was schedulable on either node. Unlike the TP=3 fp8 cell, this build pins the control plane to the QSFP fabric: NCCL/GLOO/TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp1s0f1np1 and NCCL_IB_HCA=rocep1s0f1 (verified in the serve process environment).

gotchas.text: TP=2 is two GB10 nodes over the QSFP fabric (ray head 192.168.1.11 + worker 192.168.1.2, one RDMA link pinned: NCCL_IB_HCA=rocep1s0f1), not two GPUs in one box: per-layer tensor-parallel all-reduce crosses the inter-node link, so per-request decode stays latency-bound. Compare against hardware.count=2 cells, or cross-count only with the topology in mind; the single-node nvfp4 arms (c2da0164, cb516ca) and the 3-node fp8 arm (7f6f0043) each measure a different topology.

The container is a locally built image, local/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next-ray2.57.0 (entrypoint 'ray start --head', ray 2.57.0; 'vllm serve' runs as a job inside), not the upstream vllm/vllm-openai image the 0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198 version string suggests. VLLM_MARLIN_USE_ATOMIC_ADD=1 is set in the image env (not a CLI flag) and plausibly affects MoE marlin kernel selection on sm_121.

Unlike the TP=3 fp8 arm, this build keeps the whole control plane off the 1 GbE uplink: NCCL/GLOO/TP_SOCKET_IFNAME point at enp1s0f1np1 (a 200G QSFP port) rather than the Realtek management NIC. Control-plane traffic no longer shares the box's internet path.

Speculative decoding is the model's own trained MTP head at num_speculative_tokens=4 here; the single-node nvfp4 arms on this hardware use 3. Decode throughput is not like-for-like across those cells.

Prefix caching is ON and --enforce-eager is on (no CUDA graphs) in this arm, matching the TP=3 fp8 arm; the single-node nvfp4 arms differ on both (caching off over a GDN kernel bug, PIECEWISE cudagraphs captured). serve-chat-c8 samples mostly distinct prompts so the cache is near-inert for this workload.
Telemetry (gpu_util/power/temp) is sampled on the head node only - one of the two GPUs; the worker node's sensors are not captured by this result.

provenance.notes: First nvfp4 multi-node arm for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on GB10: --tensor-parallel-size 2 with --distributed-executor-backend ray spans two DGX Sparks (head 192.168.1.11 + 192.168.1.2), so hardware.count=2. Weights are the community RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 quant, served from the container HF cache at snapshot 7b719225242aacd3dbd3f9407468c2ee9a9d2594 - byte-identical revision to the quant registry and to the single-node nvfp4 arms, so quant is controlled for when comparing against them or against the TP=3 fp8 cell (7f6f004369fd6cf7, PR #126), which is otherwise the closest config: same engine build, same seqs/mem/MTP-4/eager/prefix-caching flags, differing in quant and TP width (3 nodes + expert-parallel + mm-encoder-tp-mode there; none of those flags here). Server was already running (attach mode); harness only measured.
